artworks.title: Plate with Hypermnestra Watching Lynceus Take Her Father's Crown
artworks.description: Walters maiolica: Lynceus — the sole son of Aegyptus spared on the Danaid wedding night — seizes Danaus’ crown while Hypermnestra watches. Renaissance tin-glaze makes the Argive survivor a king-maker, not the sharp-eyed Argonaut who shares his name.

artworks.title: Hypermnestra, Lynceus, and the Danaïdes
artworks.description: Early printed woodcut of the Danaid crisis names Lynceus beside Hypermnestra — the bridegroom who lived when forty-nine brothers died. Book illustration kept the Argive pair legible for readers of Ovid’s Heroides.

popCulture.title: Heroides XIV (Hypermnestra to Lynceus)
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid’s letter is written to Lynceus from Hypermnestra’s prison — the spared husband as addressee of the Danaid who would not kill.
